stage1.impression: A warm, dark timber record-wall bar with low dome pendants and two big speakers in lit niches. The timber, fluted counter front and record spines hold up, and the exposure is right for night. What gives it away as CG is the people: four grey, untextured clay figures smeared by fake motion, with pink blobs for heads, and they take the eye before anything else. The speakers read as grey hi-fi boxes behind glass with a bright white wedge above the left one, not as glowing tinted acrylic heroes, and the zinc counter is a flat, evenly lit grey slab. As a specific place it is close (record wall, niches, fluted oak, Domes), but as framed it reads as a generic wood-panelled bar, and a magazine would not run it with these figures.

blocking_9: No figure reads as a grey untextured mannequin: people must wear real clothing materials with skin and hair, or be cut to one or two far enough back and blurred enough that only colour and motion read

The left speaker reads at a glance as tinted cast acrylic with its light inside it (edge glow and visible batts), not as a grey box behind a reflective pane, and the bright wedge above it (240-340, 150-230) is gone
The zinc top shows patina, falloff between pendant pools and real reflections of glasses, not a uniform pale grey band (region 0-900, 590-720)
The ceiling and upper right (600-1200, 0-280) show fir grain and beam modelling from bounce or a grazing light, rather than a flat brown field
A sign of the place's identity (the frosted disc, the decks, a screen) reads clearly enough that the frame could not be any wood-panelled bar

defects.what: the bartender is a grey untextured clay form with a pink sphere head and a green smear arm: reads as a placeholder mannequin, not a motion-blurred person
the selector is the same grey clay form with a pink head, and the speaker is visible through it, so it reads as a ghost overlay
the seated guest is a grey mannequin with a grey seat; the arm's smear crosses the counter like a composited streak
a hard bright white wedge (p95 224) at the top of the left niche reads as a sky or monitor reflection, the brightest non-lamp surface in the frame
the hero speaker is neutral grey (R45 G44 B49) seen through a reflective pane with vertical frame bars; no acrylic edge glow and no tint read, so it looks like a studio monitor in a cupboard
the second speaker's woofer face is brighter (median 105) than the hero's (44), so the far speaker competes with the near one
the zinc top is a flat, uniformly pale grey (p95 207) with no patina, no pools of light and only faint reflections of the glasses: reads as painted MDF or concrete
the nearest Dome's liner is near-white (median 208), cold against the 2400 K room; it reads as an opal plastic shade, not tinted smoked acrylic
the ceiling and beams are a flat dark brown (median 18, range 31): no grain, no beam modelling
the foreground chairs are smooth, uniform tan blocks with CG-clean edges and no leather grain or wear
the back right is an empty black-grey wall with two floating Domes; the far half of the room carries no story (no disc, no screen, no bottles)
slightly soft overall with a fine, even grain that reads as added in post; whites are a little green-grey against warm surroundings

changes.problem: The four people read as grey untextured clay mannequins with pink sphere heads, the single strongest CG cue in the frame.

evidence.measured: bartender median lum 100, R103 G99 B95: a uniform neutral grey with no fabric or skin variation; the selector at 720-860 is transparent over the speaker

change.from: 4 people (2 at the counter, bartender, selector), shutter 0.75 frame, head travel [0.16, 0.09, 0.03] m
change.to: 2 people: keep the selector at the decks and one seated guest, move the bartender out of the frame, cut the near-left counter figure; shutter 1.5 frames so they read as streaks of dark clothing, and give them dark wool and denim with skin tones if the figures' materials allow it; nothing grey or untextured

changes.expected: the eye goes to the speaker and the counter first; the remaining figures read as a dark, warm, moving presence, not mannequins; the bartender's grey block in front of the record wall is gone

changes.problem: The hero speaker reads as a neutral grey box behind a reflective pane, not as tinted acrylic with light inside it, and it is darker than the far speaker.

evidence.measured: median 44, R45 G44 B49 (no tint, cool); far speaker [690,320,760,500] median 105

change.setting: the lit niche's strip and the lamps on the speakers
change.from: lit niche strip 0.06; each speaker 4 x area, 1.0 W/m2, 2900 K
change.to: lit niche strip 0.15 at 2700 K, placed to graze the cabinet's polished edges from below and behind; the near (left) speaker's area lamps 2.0 W/m2 and the far one's 0.8 W/m2, so the hero is the brighter of the two

changes.expected: the left cabinet's edges glow, the smoke tint and white batts read through the acrylic, and the near speaker becomes brighter than the far one

changes.problem: A hard white wedge at the top of the left niche, an environment or screen reflection, is the brightest non-lamp surface and pulls the eye off the speaker.

change.setting: the screens' brightness and the niche's glazing (what reflects there)
change.from: screens' images 0.016; whatever bright source reflects into the niche's upper pane
change.to: find the source (likely a screen or the street side) and drop it to 0.006, or angle the camera 2 deg left so the reflection leaves the pane

changes.expected: the top of the niche goes to dark timber, with no bright wedge

changes.problem: The zinc counter is a flat, uniformly pale grey band that reads as painted board, with no patina and no pools under the pendants.

evidence.measured: p95 207, a uniform pale field from x 0 to 900; no falloff between the Domes

change.setting: the zinc's patina and the Domes' downlights
change.from: clean zinc, a broad sheen; downlights 16 W, cone 20 deg
change.to: darker blue-grey zinc with mottled oxidation, rings and wipe marks (base 0.25 albedo, roughness 0.3 to 0.55 varied); downlights 22 W at cone 14 deg so each makes a distinct pool on the counter, with darker zinc between

changes.expected: pools of warm light on the zinc under each Dome with clear falloff between them, and the glasses reflected in a metal that reads as old zinc

changes.problem: The Dome liners glow near-white and cold, reading as opal plastic shades rather than smoked acrylic, and they are the frame's brightest objects.

evidence.measured: median 208, R205 G208 B209 (neutral to cool against a 2700 K grade)

change.to: 0.002, with the liner's emission at 2400 K

changes.expected: the shades read as warm smoked acrylic glowing from inside, bright but no longer white

changes.problem: The far right of the frame and the ceiling are flat dark fields that carry no detail and nothing specific to the place.

evidence.measured: median 36, an empty grey-black wall; ceiling [600,0,1200,280] median 18, range 31

change.setting: the disc behind the DJ station and the record wall's spots
change.from: disc 0.06 in #FFC890 with a 4.0 W area lamp; record wall 4 x 8 W, cone 26 deg
change.to: disc 0.12 with an 8 W area lamp so its warm glow grazes the beams; record wall 10 W, with one spot aimed up to wash the fir ceiling at 15 % of its output

changes.expected: the beams show fir grain and modelling and the back of the room carries a warm glow that identifies it as this bar

changes.problem: The foreground chairs are smooth, uniform tan blocks with CG-clean edges.

evidence.measured: seen at 2x: no grain or creasing, a uniform tan with a single soft highlight

change.to: aged cognac leather: a pebble-grain normal at 1 mm scale, roughness 0.45 to 0.65, darker at the seams with wear on the arm tops; take the base down one stop

changes.expected: the chairs read as worn leather furniture and stop pulling the eye to the corner

changes.problem: The whites drift green-grey and the even grain over the soft image reads as added in post.

evidence.measured: R103 G105 B109: cool against the 2700 K room

change.setting: render: white_balance_tint and the finish's grain
change.to: white_balance_tint +2.0, with the grain halved and tied to luminance (more in the shadows, none in the highlights)

changes.expected: neutral-to-warm whites with no green cast, and grain that reads as film or sensor

out_of_scope.request: Make the smoked speaker read with more colour, so it is the one saturated thing in the frame
out_of_scope.why: the configuration (Smoke) and the speaker's tint are fixed; with smoked products the frame has no saturated hero colour by design, so the hero must be carried by light and placement instead (c2)

out_of_scope.request: Remove the reflective pane and the vertical frame bars in front of the left speaker in its niche
out_of_scope.why: the niches and their glazing are part of the room's fixed design; only the reflections and light can be managed (c3)

out_of_scope.request: Replace the people with real scanned humans or dressed figures
out_of_scope.why: the people are fixed in kind; only their number, places and blur may change, and clothing materials only if the asset allows it
